a: Fields of an aliased object leaf are tagged by the target's path, but `panelMarkedPaths` answers with the alias's key, so marks and tab leads never reach them
`panelSource` keeps one PanelLeaf per path, so `stateAt` and reset gating answer for whichever leaf sharing a path came last
`sharedRows` pairs an object's fields across a section, but `fieldPairs` (which draws them) ends a run at a section
Top-level leaves are paired across the sections between them; nested leaves are not
b: An action field of an object leaf never draws pressed in a selection panel: `leafContext` hands no `activeAt`
`panelSource` indexes leaves by `path`, so two leaves sharing a path (an alias and its target, or two aliases) answer each other's state and reset
`panelMarkedPaths` pairs an object leaf's fields across section boundaries and inside bars, where `ObjectLeaf` draws them apart
An alias of an object leaf is marked under its own key but its fields are drawn under the target's path
Across several kinds, every node is read, bounded, written and reset under the first kind's leaf
A glyph-named flag toggle in an object leaf's paired row takes an even share of the row
